# How Erasure Coding Reconstructs Missing Storage Shards

Erasure coding is a mathematical technique for storing data across multiple storage locations (shards) such that the data can be recovered even if some shards are lost. It is the backbone of modern distributed storage systems—HDFS RAID, Ceph, Backblaze, Amazon S3's durability model, and countless others—because it achieves far better durability per byte of overhead than simple replication. This essay explains the reconstruction mechanism, walks through concrete worked examples, and discusses the practical limitations that constrain real-world deployments.
